Bina Rani and another ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Shantosh Chandra Dey ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 8. Mr. MA Wahab Miah, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submits that the deceased plaintiff Hiron Chandra Dey took pattan of 0.63 acres of land from Haru Chandra Datta on payment of a salami of Taka 300.00 on the basis of pattanirukka dated 14 Chaitra 1353 BS and purchased by different kabalas from 25-1-48 to 20- 11-50 rest of the property of schedule 1, in total 2.82 acres of land, in the benami of his minor son defendant No.1 who was born on 29-5-42. He took further settlement of schedule 2 land measuring 0.93 acres with his own money and for his own benefit and interest from Kiron Chandra on payment of najar salami of Taka 1000.00 on the basis of a pattanirukka on 17 Jaistha 1362 BS corresponding to 1st July 1956 in the benami of his minor sons defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Defendant No. 2 was born on 27-3-51. The plaintiff by examining his wife, the mother of defendant No. 1 (PW 6) and his mother-in-law, the grandmother of defendant No. 1 (PW 7) positively proved the requirements of benami transaction i.e. sources of money for purchasing and taking settlement of the disputed land, custody of the documents, continuous possession of the property, etc. which the trial Court upon a detailed consideration of the evidence on record found in favour of the plaintiff and accordingly, decreed the suit; but the learned Judges of the High Court Division committed a gross error of law in dismissing partly the suit upon taking an erroneous view of law that the suit would fail because the plaintiff had failed to prove the alleged intention or motive behind his benami purchase /settlement. Learned Advocate further submits that the High Court Division failed to take into consideration that at the time of first purchase, a part of the schedule 1 land in the year 1948, defendant No.1 was aged about 6 years and at the time of last purchase of a part of schedule land in 1950 defendant No.1 was aged about 8 years and that PW 7 Kamini Sundari Dey positively supported the case of the plaintiff and did not at all support the case of defendant No 1, that the suit property is a self-acquired property of defendant No.1 through her. The High Court Division upon taking an untenable view of the law of benami transaction wrongly held that because the plaintiff had failed to prove the intention or motive behind the benami transaction the suit will fail in respect of schedule 1 property. The learned Advocate also submits that the High Court Division without any application of mind as to the facts and circumstances of the case dismissed the suit in part holding inter alia, that "the 2nd defendant influenced the plaintiff to institute the suit and that there was no motive in which the plaintiff would purchase schedule 1 land in the benami of defendant and that the plea of benami was an afterthought".
